rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Le Chatelier's principle is chemistry's thermostat: disturb an equilibrium and it moves to **oppose** you. **Concentration** changes shift toward consuming what you added (or restoring what you removed) — the arithmetic behind Qc falling below or rising above Kc.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "When a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, temperature or pressure, the system shifts its equilibrium position to counteract the effect of the change."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The two NEB answers*** — 2024's pressure question: count 4 gas moles left, 2 right, shift forward. 2022's temperature question: ΔH positive means heat sits on the reactant side, so added heat drives forward and the brown deepens. Two questions, one principle, opposite directions.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Rule That Runs the Chemical Industry Le Chatelier's principle (1888) predicts which way an equilibrium moves when conditions change: the system shifts to **oppose** the change. One sentence decides the Haber process's pressure, the contact process's temperature, and the marks on every equilibrium question — including two verified NEB sets (2024 and 2022) solved below.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The principle - **Statement:** when a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, pressure (volume), or temperature, the equilibrium shifts in the direction that tends to **reduce (oppose) the effect** of that change. - It is qualitative — it predicts direction, never the new Kc (which only temperature alters).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Mole count first: fewer gas moles wins under pressure. Heat on the reactant side = endothermic = heating drives forward. "Only T changes Kc" - write it in every answer. Colour cue: NO2 brown, N2O4 colourless.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Verified NEB 2024 (3m): State Le Chatelier's principle. Predict the effect of increasing pressure on the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g).** — **Principle:** when a change is imposed on a system at equilibrium (change in concentration, pressure or temperature), the equilibrium shifts in the direction that tends to oppose or nullify…  ·  **Verified NEB 2022 (2m): For the equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), ΔH = +57 kJ mol⁻¹. State and explain the effect of increasing temperature on this equilibrium.** — Since ΔH is positive, the forward reaction (N₂O₄ → 2NO₂) is **endothermic** and the reverse is exothermic.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For full marks pair the shift with its reason ("fewer moles opposes the compression") and state the observable (more NH3 / deeper brown) — prediction plus explanation is the NEB pattern.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Heat is a participant: write it on the exothermic product side (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ + heat) or the endothermic reactant side (N₂O₄ + heat ⇌ 2NO₂) and every temperature question becomes reading the equation.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Principle: equilibrium shifts to OPPOSE the imposed change (concentration/pressure/temperature). Concentration: add reactant/remove product -> forward; reverse -> backward. Pressure: toward fewer gas moles (dn = 0: no effect; inert gas at constant V: no effect).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Haemoglobin's oxygen loading is Le Chatelier in the bloodstream: at high altitude, lower O₂ partial pressure shifts the equilibrium toward release — the body compensates with more haemoglobin (concentration shift, the mountaineers' polycythaemia).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): In the Haber process, ammonia is continuously removed by liquefaction. Explain, using Le Chatelier's principle, why this increases the yield.** — Removing the product NH₃ decreases its concentration, so the reaction quotient Qc = [NH₃]²/([N₂][H₂]³) falls below Kc.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Why is the contact process run at ~450 °C rather than at 25 °C despite the exothermic ΔH?  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Pressure acts on gas moles, not molecules' weight:** count moles of gas only — solids and liquids (CaCO₃ ⇌ CaO + CO₂: Δn = +1 from gases alone) are invisible to pressure.  ·  **Heating helps endothermic, not "everything":** students shift every reaction forward on heating; the direction is decided by which side absorbs the heat.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Temperature is special:** concentration and pressure changes move the position but leave Kc untouched; only temperature writes a new Kc — mixing this up loses both reasoning marks.  ·  ## 7.
